statement: Directed Steiner arborescence (Dreyfus-Wagner DP) outperforms undirected Steiner tree approximation on inter-cloud broadcast configs by 6.6% per-config cost reduction, due to asymmetric edge costs (75% of edges differ by up to 7.3x between forward/reverse). Intra-provider configs show no improvement because within-provider edges have near-symmetric costs.
regime: Inter-cloud broadcast configurations with cross-provider edge cost asymmetry; graph size n=71, terminals k<=7 (tractable for exact DP)
mechanism: The undirected Steiner tree minimizes cost on min(forward, reverse) edge weights, but actual routing from src must follow directed edges. For inter-cloud configs, cross-provider edges have high asymmetry (e.g., aws:af-south-1 to aws:us-east-2 = $0.147 vs reverse $0.02). The directed DP selects edges where the routing direction is genuinely cheap, saving $11.36 per inter-cloud config.
applicability_bounds: Applies when edge cost asymmetry is significant (>5% of edges with >2x forward/reverse ratio) and graph + terminal count is tractable for Dreyfus-Wagner DP (O(3^k * n + 2^k * n^2)). Does not apply to intra-provider configs where edge costs are near-symmetric.

statement: Instance cost from relay nodes in the Steiner tree partially offsets egress savings. The treatment score (0.1341) was lower than the probe estimate (0.154), suggesting transfer-time-induced instance cost is non-negligible when relay paths create bandwidth bottlenecks.
regime: Superseded — iter-2 showed instance cost is only ~1.5% of total ($10 out of $650), and the iter-1 score discrepancy was an implementation bug, not instance cost.
mechanism: Original mechanism was correct in direction but wrong in magnitude. Instance cost is negligible.
applicability_bounds: No longer applicable — see RP-3 for current understanding.
